title: QR Code Phishing (Quishing) Explained
summary: Quishing occurs when attackers place malicious QR codes over legitimate ones (e.g. at parking meters, restaurants, or in emails) to redirect victims to credential-harvesting websites or initiate malicious intents.
defenseGuidance: Always preview the destination domain before opening links from QR codes. Check for tampering stickers on physical QR displays and inspect sanitized destination protocols.

title: Internationalized Domain Name (IDN) Homoglyph Attacks
summary: Attackers register domain names using lookalike characters from Cyrillic, Greek, or Latin alphabets (prefixed by 'xn--' in ASCII) to spoof well-known brand names like apple.com, google.com, or paypal.com.
defenseGuidance: Inspect the raw Punycode domain for 'xn--' prefixes. Verify the domain security certificate and look for slight font rendering variations in the browser address bar.

title: Wi-Fi Airspace Encryption Standards & Rogue Access Points
summary: Open and unencrypted 802.11 networks transmit frames in cleartext that can be captured by local packet sniffers. Rogue Access Points (Evil Twins) mimic trusted network names to conduct man-in-the-middle attacks.
defenseGuidance: Prefer WPA3-SAE or WPA2 networks with 802.11w Protected Management Frames. Always enable an encrypted VPN tunnel when accessing untrusted public or hotel hotspots.

title: Mobile App Permissions & Telemetry Data Harvesting
summary: Overprivileged mobile apps requesting background location, contacts, SMS, or microphone access can covertly track user movements and sell device telemetry to third-party data brokers.
defenseGuidance: Grant sensitive permissions only 'While using the app'. Routinely audit and revoke permissions for apps that have not been used recently using on-device privacy tools.

title: URL Shortener Concealment & Redirection Chains
summary: Shortener services (bit.ly, tinyurl.com, t.co) obscure the true destination URL, making it impossible for users to visually assess whether a link directs to a credential phishing page or malware payload.
defenseGuidance: Always expand shortened URLs or inspect them using automated link sandboxes before opening. Avoid entering credentials following multi-hop HTTP redirections.

title: Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing Principles
summary: Ethical hacking involves authorized, legal security assessments to identify, report, and remediate vulnerabilities before malicious threat actors can exploit them. Practitioners employ red teaming, fuzzing, static code analysis, and sandbox execution under strict rules of engagement.
defenseGuidance: Adopt continuous vulnerability management, enforce least-privilege access, mandate code audits, and implement bug bounty programs to harden defenses against real-world adversaries.

title: 802.11 Deauthentication Attacks & Evil Twin Jamming
summary: Attackers transmit spoofed 802.11 deauthentication management frames to disconnect clients from legitimate access points, compelling the victim's device to auto-connect to a rogue Evil Twin hotspot with identical SSID.
defenseGuidance: Ensure your router supports and enforces 802.11w Protected Management Frames (PMF) which cryptographically sign management frames, rendering deauth attacks ineffective.

title: Phishing & Social Engineering Manipulation
summary: Phishing exploits cognitive biases and emotional urgency to trick victims into revealing sensitive credentials, private OTP tokens, or downloading weaponized attachments disguised as trusted organizations.
defenseGuidance: Never click unsolicited urgent verification links. Verify communications out-of-band by directly typing the official organization website into your browser.

title: SMS OTP Interception & SIM Swapping Fraud
summary: Attackers deceive mobile telecom carriers into porting a victim's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM card, enabling interception of one-time passwords (OTPs) and account takeover.
defenseGuidance: Transition from SMS-based OTP verification to hardware FIDO2 security keys (YubiKey) or time-based authenticator apps (TOTP like Google Authenticator). Set a PIN on your cellular account.

title: Ransomware & Weaponized Malware Payloads
summary: Ransomware covertly encrypts critical storage files and databases using asymmetric cryptography, demanding cryptocurrency ransoms for decryption keys. Infection vectors include malicious email attachments and drive-by downloads.
defenseGuidance: Maintain immutable 3-2-1 offline backups, enforce software patching, disable legacy macro execution, and restrict executable permissions on untrusted downloads.

title: Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) & SSL Stripping Attacks
summary: MITM attacks occur when an adversary intercepts communications between two endpoints. SSL stripping forces secure HTTPS connections to downgrade to cleartext HTTP, exposing credentials and session cookies.
defenseGuidance: Enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) with preloading in browsers. Disconnect immediately if browser displays certificate invalidity warnings or protocol downgrade notices.

title: Zero-Trust Architecture & Continuous Verification
summary: Zero-Trust security operates on the core principle: 'Never Trust, Always Verify'. Every access request—regardless of origin within or outside the network perimeter—must be authenticated, authorized, and cryptographically verified.
defenseGuidance: Implement continuous posture verification, least-privilege microsegmentation, end-to-end encryption for all data in transit, and multi-factor authentication across all endpoints.
